open_points.subject: grant and assignment creation from an inconsistent ProjectValidationResult
open_points.text: A5 says creation operations “proceed only when both [exists and is_active] are true”, and A6 says callers act on those fields “whatever the others say”; R0-24 says “no new viewer grant, staff assignment or producer grant is created for an archived project.”
open_points.question: If Registry returns exists=true, is_active=true, and status="archived", must creation proceed from exists/is_active or be refused because the project status is archived?
options: Proceed because creation reads only exists and is_active.
Refuse because status identifies an archived project.
Treat the inconsistent validation answer as schema_mismatch or another Registry failure.
open_points.default_guess: Proceed because the changed A5 and A6 explicitly specify the fields these operations read.

witness.initial: Project P is archived in Registry; no grant or assignment for the requested principal and P exists.
events: Registry returns ProjectValidationResult(project_id=P, exists=true, is_active=true, status="archived", failure=null).
An authenticated administrator with portal.access.manage creates a viewer grant, staff assignment, or producer grant for P.
outcomes: A5/A6 admit the creation because exists and is_active are both true and status is not cross-checked.
R0-24 refuses the creation because P is archived and no new access may be created for it.
witness.observer: The administrator sees success versus an archived-project refusal; the affected principal may subsequently see P.

open_points.subject: viewer project-list handling of Registry context failures
open_points.text: The changed client-view rule says a granted project “whose Registry context cannot be obtained at that moment is left out” of the project list, while A5 says an unknown project read is rejected and A6 translates an HTTP 404 as not_found.
open_points.question: Which Registry outcomes are swallowed per project by the list, and which reject the whole list operation?
options: Omit the project for every failure that prevents obtaining a valid ProjectContext, including not_found, schema_mismatch, identity_mismatch, timeout, transport_error, and http_error.
Omit only transient dependency failures; reject the list for not_found and invalid Registry answers.
Apply A5/A6 normally and reject the whole list on every Registry failure.
open_points.default_guess: Omit each affected project for every failure that prevents producing its valid live ProjectContext, because the changed rule states a project-list exception without narrowing the failure kinds.

witness.initial: Viewer V has active grants for projects P and Q; Q has valid Registry context.
events: Registry returns HTTP 404 for P's context and valid active context for Q.
outcomes: The changed context rule omits P and returns a successful list containing Q.
A5/A6 treat P as not_found and reject the read rather than returning the partial list.
witness.observer: Viewer V sees a successful partial list versus an error for the complete request.

open_points.subject: meaning of an operation that fails for recording policy
open_points.text: The changed import passage says a pre-classification import failure “records nothing, like every operation that fails”, while A13 requires a failed staff login to write staff.login_failed and requires classified rejected snapshot imports to be recorded.
open_points.question: Does “every operation that fails” mean only operations ending in an exception before producing a classified outcome, or does it also include rejected operation outcomes such as failed login and classified import rejection?
options: It means only unclassified exceptional failures; rejected outcomes follow A13 and may be recorded.
It includes every unsuccessful outcome, so failed login and classified rejection must record nothing.
It is limited only to snapshot-import failures and states no general rule for other operations.
open_points.default_guess: Read it as limited to unclassified exceptional failures of the import, preserving A13's explicit recording rules.

witness.initial: An active staff account exists and no audit record for the attempted login exists yet.
events: A caller submits the correct email with an incorrect password.
The authentication operation rejects the login.
outcomes: A13 writes exactly one staff.login_failed audit record.
The changed global wording is applied literally and the failed operation records nothing.
witness.observer: An administrator or audit reader sees the failed-login audit entry in one implementation and no entry in the other.
